item.content:encoded:
The local networking group, Ladies Out Lunching – LOL for short – will host their July Luncheon at Lost Pizza Company in Benton, Wednesday, August 19th from 12:00 – 1:00 pm. 

Come ready to chat and make some new friends! 

Luncheon Details:

– Lunch is Dutch Treat: just order and pay your meal.

– Don’t forget to bring your business cards and materials!

– Happy Gift: If you would like a minute to share about your business bring a small gift or some business swag to share! We will draw for a recipient and you get a chance to share – everyone loves a present… right?

NONPROFIT SUPPORT! This month we are collecting nonperishable food items and feminine hygiene products for local food pantries.

LOL meets the 3rd Wednesday of each month at various restaurants around Saline County.  Learn more about LOL and RSVP to an event by visiting  www.facebook.com/groups/ladiesoutlunching/

item.title: Saline County Flea Market and Trade Day is set for Aug 15th at Fairgrounds
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: The Saline County Fair Association is hosting its fourth Flea Market and Trade Day on Saturday, August 15, offering a diverse array of local merchandise, crafts, and food. Proceeds from this free event will directly fund ongoing efforts to rebuild and improve the Saline County Fairgrounds. Read more below. The community fundraiser, themed “Rebuilding Together,” […]
item.content:encoded:
The Saline County Fair Association is hosting its fourth Flea Market and Trade Day on Saturday, August 15, offering a diverse array of local merchandise, crafts, and food.

Proceeds from this free event will directly fund ongoing efforts to rebuild and improve the Saline County Fairgrounds. Read more below.




The community fundraiser, themed “Rebuilding Together,” is 7:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at the Fairgrounds, at 406 Fairfield in Benton. The event will take place rain or shine, because the indoor vendor buildings are fully air-conditioned.

Shoppers can expect to find a wide variety of goods, including:

  • yard sale items,
  • flea market finds,
  • crafts,
  • antiques,
  • fresh produce,
  • eggs,
  • animals, and
  • animal supplies.

Come hungry,  because the Homemakers Extension kitchen and concession stand will be open, serving a variety of foods and treats to raise additional funds for the rebuilding project.

If you’d like to be a vendor, indoor and outdoor vendor spaces are still available. A 12×12-foot outside space costs $25, while a 10×10-foot inside space is $50. The spaces do not include tents, tables, chairs, electricity, or water, and all booth rental proceeds go directly toward the fairgrounds.

Vendor setup is scheduled for Friday evening from 4:30-7:00 p.m., and Saturday morning at 6:00 a.m. Participating businesses are required to meet all standard licensing requirements, and animal vendors must comply with applicable regulations.

Upcoming Flea Market and Trade Days are scheduled for September 26, October 24, and a two-day event on November 6 and 7. Interested vendors or attendees can request  information by texting 501-860-3101, emailing salinecofair@hotmail.com, or visiting the association’s online registration form.

item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: Registration is officially open for the annual Saline County 9/11 Memorial Stair Climb & Walk, to take place at the Benton Panthers Athletics Complex. The community-wide event invites firefighters, first responders, and residents to climb in remembrance of those who lost their lives in the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. Read more below. item.content:encoded:
Registration is officially open for the annual Saline County 9/11 Memorial Stair Climb & Walk, to take place at the Benton Panthers Athletics Complex. The community-wide event invites firefighters, first responders, and residents to climb in remembrance of those who lost their lives in the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. Read more below.




The memorial climb will take place on Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026, at the Benton High School athletics complex located at 1800 Benton Parkway in Benton.

Participants will gather to pay tribute to the 343 FDNY firefighters, 71 police officers, eight EMS personnel, and all the civilians who perished on September 11, 2001.

Proceeds from the event will benefit the National Fallen Firefighters Foundation (NFFF). The foundation uses these funds to support programs honoring fallen American firefighters, as well as to assist their families and departments in times of need.

The schedule for the morning of September 12 is as follows:

  • Onsite Registration: 8:00 a.m.
  • Opening Ceremony: 8:30 a.m.
  • Stair Climb & Walk Start: 9:00 a.m.
  • Climb End: 11:00 a.m.

The event is open to the entire community. Organizers are urging participants to begin now in training and preparing. Online registration will close at midnight on Friday, Sept. 11. Participants can sign up through the National Fallen Firefighters Foundation’s official page at nfff.akaraisin.com/ui/saline26.

For questions or further information regarding the event, residents can contact Michael York at 501-772-6929 or visit the official Facebook event page.

item.title: How the Ball Bounces with Bekka: Nobody Wins the First Practice
item.dc:creator: Bekka Wilkerson
item.category: How the Ball Bounces with Bekka
item.description: Back to school has always been one of my favorite times of the year. While it marks the first official end of summer – something I don’t necessarily relish – it also brings around a whole world of new beginnings. New shoes. New Outfits. New Backpacks. item.content:encoded:
Back to school has always been one of my favorite times of the year. While it marks the first official end of summer – something I don’t necessarily relish – it also brings around a whole world of new beginnings.  

New shoes. New Outfits.  New Backpacks.  The anticipation of a new school year.

But also…a fresh uniform…striped fields…the sound of a basketball bouncing and the smell of the freshly refinished hardwood floor.

Whistles that have been hanging silent all summer finally finding their way back around a coach’s neck. Parents unfolding lawn chairs they swear they put away just a few weeks ago.

And kids…kids who somehow grew three inches since school let out.

Across Arkansas this week, athletes are walking into their first practices of a brand-new season.

Some are excited.

Some are nervous.

Some are wondering if they still remember how to play.

Some are wondering if they belong at all.

And every single one of them is starting in exactly the same place.

Practice.

Not a championship. Not a playoff game. Not Senior Night.

Practice.

The funny thing is…nobody wins the first practice.

There isn’t a trophy waiting at the end. Nobody hangs a banner because everybody survived day one of conditioning, or what feels like day 5000 of conditioning.

Nobody earns a state championship because they had a great August.

The first practice isn’t about proving anything. It’s about preparing for everything.

I remember that feeling.  Even though it was our “job” to stay in the groove all summer with conditioning and shooting, walking into the gym after a summer away always brought a mix of coming home and apprehension.  

Wondering if my shot would still be there…if I had done enough during the offseason…would Coach think I had done enough in the off season…

Because here’s the truth every athlete eventually learns: The season doesn’t begin on opening night. It begins long before anyone is keeping score. It begins in ordinary practices.

In line drills.

In stretching.

In learning names.

In figuring out who encourages teammates…and who hangs their head when things get hard.

READ MORE BELOW




The first practice tells you almost nothing about how the season will end but everything about who you are and who you will become as a team as the season progresses.

I’ve seen kids struggle through the first week of practice and become incredible players by the end of the year. I’ve seen the most naturally talented athletes lose their spot because they lost their fire and stopped putting in the work. And I’ve seen teammates who barely played become the heart of a team simply because everyone knew they could be counted on.

The first practice doesn’t reveal talent nearly as much as it reveals attitude.

The older I’ve gotten, the more I’ve realized life gives us first practices all the time.

The first day at a new job.

The first board meeting.

The first day of school.

The first time you volunteer.

The first time you decide to get healthy.

The first conversation after deciding to repair a relationship.

None of those moments determine the outcome, they simply mark the beginning. What really matters is what happens after everyone else goes home.

The showing up.

The consistency.

The willingness to keep coming back when the excitement wears off and the work begins. Because that’s when seasons are really built.

Not under Friday night lights. Not in championship games. Not when everybody is watching. But on ordinary afternoons…when nobody is keeping score.

Maybe that’s why nobody wins the first practice.

The victory isn’t in what happens that day.

The victory is deciding you’ll come back tomorrow.

And the next day.

And the day after that.

Because championships are never won in the first practice. But they can absolutely be lost by deciding it wasn’t important.

And that’s how the ball really bounces.

Read more from How the Ball Bounces with Bekka in the archives at www.mysaline.com/bounces.

About the author: Bekka Wilkerson is a lifelong lover of all things sports. Raised in a super athletic household it was no surprise when she too began to love sports at a young age. It seems like from the time she could walk she had a softball bat in her hands, but her true athletic passion came from all things Basketball. That love served her well as a Bryant High School Lady Hornet and ultimately earned her a full scholarship to play at the University of Central Arkansas – among many other adventures.
These days Bekka can be found running around Saline County with her husband, Speedy, or chasing one of her grandsons. She is also the Executive Director of The EMpact One Foundation, a Saline County Nonprofit Organization that helps young people stay connected to extracurricular activities through tuition assistance and equipment provisions.
